Subject: 5/5 — Fast, careful work that kept our Palomar run on schedule

Arroyo Precision Works made a camera-to-dewar adapter plate and an internally threaded light baffle tube for our near-IR camera (PO 26-41187). Both parts were 6061-T6 aluminum with black anodizing. A larger vendor quoted us six weeks for the job. Arroyo quoted 21 days and delivered the finished parts only nine days after the PO. That gave us time for a proper fit test before our Palomar 200-inch run beginning November 18, instead of spending the week before the run worrying about whether I could use the camera.

The speed was great, but the main reason I am leaving this review is how carefully they handled the drawing. During setup, Tiff noticed that the bolt circle on sheet 2 was listed as 4.125 even though the other dimensions on that drawing were in millimeters. Ruben contacted me before cutting and asked whether it should be 4.125 inches, or 104.8 mm, rather than 4.125 mm. Machining it literally as 4.125 mm would have put the screws inside the bore.

I want to be clear that this mistake was mine, not Arroyo’s. I had copied the dimension from an old drawing for the previous camera and left it in inches. They could have simply followed the drawing, but instead someone actually looked at how the dimensions related to the part and stopped to check. That question probably saved the plate and prevented a serious delay to our observing run.

The parts also passed my fit test without any rework. All eight screws holding the plate to the dewar went in without forcing. Flatness across the face measured under 0.01 mm on the dial indicator. The baffle threads ran smoothly, and a 300-second dark frame with the lab lights on showed no light leak—the result was the same as with the closed dewar. The black anodizing was even, with no bare spots, and the parts came back with an inspection sheet after passing Arroyo’s inspection.

Ruben’s communication was straightforward and helpful throughout. When the parts returned from anodizing, he personally brought them to the Robinson Lab loading dock, at no charge, because he was already heading toward a supplier in Glendale. After everything that had gone into getting the camera ready, I was so relieved to receive them that I almost hugged him.

For other labs and for purchasing: this was not just a shop accepting a rush order and happening to finish quickly. Arroyo caught a consequential drawing error, confirmed it before machining, delivered well ahead of their quoted lead time, and supplied parts that fit and performed correctly the first time. I would happily use them again for prototype or short-run instrument parts, particularly when the drawing needs careful attention and the schedule is real. Five stars, and I strongly recommend adding Arroyo to the preferred-vendor list.
